content:
elaine: heads up — we've got a sustained GPU pool saturation in us-west-2. queue depth >95% for ~45m, admission started returning 429s, and fallback routing spilled traffic to eu-west which then spiked. anyone oncall? :fire:

raj: on it. seeing same in dashboards — per-route admissions jumped at 02:11 UTC. link: https://dash.reedemo/internal/metrics?graph=us-west-2-queue-depth

elaine: admission-controller logs show repeated rejects with reason=pool_capacity_exhausted. token-level traces show lots of short-running chat requests cycling.

mario: fyi — cost-sweeper job triggered an aggressive scale-down in us-west-2 at 01:50 UTC. it removed 6 reserved GPUs (policy window=30m). not sure if that overlapped with traffic pattern.

sre-oncall: confirmed — I temporarily bumped admission thresholds and enabled reserved-burst (30m) for us-west-2 to drain queue. observing lower reject rate now but eu-west still elevated due to spillover.

ingest-bot: ALERT: gpu_pool_utilization/us-west-2 > 90% (01:58 UTC)

deploy-bot: Notice: control-plane rollout (routing-controller v2.8.1) started at 02:10 UTC in us-west-2. rollout completed 02:14 UTC.

raj: putting pieces together: cost-sweeper scale-down + normal morning traffic spike + routing-controller rollout (which briefly thrashed leader leases) = admission cascade. fallback routing amplified load across regions.

elaine: code-level snippet from admission controller logs:
```text
admission_controller.go: reject=1 pool=us-west-2 reason=pool_capacity_exhausted ts=2026-03-18T02:12:34Z
admission_controller.go: fallback_route=eu-west-1 routed=120
```

mario: also saw kube scheduler churn as pods were evicted then re-admitted when autoscaler reacted. that increased control-plane CPU and contributed to slower health check responses.

sre-oncall: mitigation timeline: 02:12 bumped reserved-burst + disabled cost-sweeper autoscale for us-west-2; 02:20 rolled back routing-controller to v2.8.0; 02:25 admission rejects fell below 5/min.

raj: proposed immediate actions: 1) add a circuit-breaker on cross-region fallback so a saturated region doesn't push unlimited load elsewhere; 2) change cost-sweeper to respect min-reserved for 2h after any scale-down; 3) make routing-controller rollouts staggered by region.

elaine: agreed. also want a temporary knob to enforce backpressure at the ingress proxy (reject upstream-trips earlier) — cheaper than spinning up new GPUs quickly.

mario: filed ISSUE-3487 for cost-sweeper change and PR-5629 to add min-reserved window. link: https://git.reedemo/infra/ISSUE-3487

sre-oncall: we need a short postmortem doc and an owner. timeline + data from token traces + admission logs. who's owning?

elaine: I'll own the postmortem and coordinate the mitigations. will draft and cc infra/product for the routing changes. :white_check_mark: 

raj: thanks — let's add an action to add synthetic traffic tests during scale-down windows so we catch amplification earlier.

mario: noted. will prioritize the PR for min-reserved window.

sre-oncall: closing incident channel for realtime ops. please add follow-up items to the incident tracker.

elaine: will post the postmortem link here when ready. thanks all.
